name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 331 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 331 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Opposition leaders and journalists were detained after marching to the Supreme Court and confronting police barricades in Delhi, while four men were killed by a landmine near the LoC in the Poonch area of Azad Kashmir. In Rajouri, a teenager died after his vehicle plunged off the road. In Manipur, the Border Security Force director general reviewed the security situation and operational preparedness amid fresh violence, and the state chief minister met with BJP legislators to discuss security and development priorities. The conflict continues across Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist-affected belt, with 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Opposisjonsledere og journalister ble arrestert etter å ha marsjert til Høyesterett og konfrontert politibarikader i Delhi, mens fire menn ble drept av en landmine nær LoC i Poonch-området i Azad Kashmir. I Rajouri døde en tenåring etter at kjøretøyet hans falt av veien. I Manipur gjennomgikk Border Security Force-direktøren sikkerhetssituasjonen og operasjonell beredskap etter ny vold, og delstatsministeren møtte BJP-lovgivere for å diskutere sikkerhets- og utviklingsprioriteringer. Konflikten fortsetter i Kashmir, Manipur og i den maoist-påvirkede beltet, med 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
